text: Jacen Solo is a fictional character in the Star Wars Legends continuity, the son of Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo, nephew of Luke Skywalker, and brother of Jaina Solo and Anakin Solo, as well as cousin of Ben Skywalker. He is a central figure in several novels, especially the New Jedi Order series, and becomes the antagonist of the Legacy of the Force series under the name Darth Caedus. Created for Timothy Zahn's Thrawn trilogy, set five years after Return of the Jedi, Jacen is introduced in the 1991 novel Heir to the Empire as one of a pair of twins Leia is pregnant with, born five minutes after his sister Jaina on Coruscant in the 1993 novel The Last Command. The twins, along with their younger brother Anakin, are sent to safe havens under the protection of Leia's handmaiden, Winter. In Jedi Search, they return to Coruscant at age three and have adventures, including becoming lost in the underworld of Imperial City with C-3PO before being rescued. In The Crystal Star, all three children are abducted by Hethrir, who attempts to brainwash them into becoming Dark Jedi, but they defeat him. In the Young Jedi Knights series, Jacen travels to Yavin 4 for Jedi training, discovers a strong connection to the Living Force, communicates with jungle creatures, keeps a menagerie of animals in his room at the Great Massassi Temple, and befriends the Wookiee Lowbacca and the warrior princess Tenel Ka. In Heirs of the Force and Shadow Academy, they discover a crashed TIE fighter from the Battle of Yavin, fix it with Jaina, and are captured by its pilot Qorl, who lives in the jungle for two decades; they escape, but Qorl also escapes and later discovers the Shadow Academy, a Dark Jedi training ground led by Brakiss and containing the remains of the Dathomiri Nightsisters. The twins and their friends are kidnapped by the Second Imperium, resist the dark side, and are rescued by Luke Skywalker and Tenel Ka. After returning to Coruscant, they reunite with Zekk, fight him several times, and eventually build their first lightsabers, with Jacen using a corusca gem for his focusing crystal. In Lightsabers, Tenel Ka's lightsaber shorts out during a sparring match with Jacen when his blade passes through thin air, severing her arm, causing Jacen to suffer guilt. In Darkest Knight, they visit Kashyyyk with Lowbacca to witness his sister's rites; in Jedi Under Siege, they defeat the Shadow Academy and the Second Imperium on Yavin 4. Throughout the series, Jacen and Jaina continue training, meet new friends like Raynar Thul, and cannot convince Zekk to stay at the Academy. They discover the Diversity Alliance, an alien anti-human group led by Twi'lek Nolaa Tarkona, sister of Oola, who was murdered by Jabba the Hutt in Return of the Jedi. In Jedi Bounty, they are briefly held captive on Ryloth to rescue Lowbacca, who joined the Diversity Alliance; in The Emperor's Plague, they uncover a plot involving General Evir Derricote's deadly diseases hidden in an Imperial storehouse, defeat Tarkona, who dies from one of the plagues, and Bornan Thul dies from the plague before his son's eyes. In Return to Ord Mantell, they visit the planet to watch a race, encounter Czethros, a bounty hunter who once hunted Han, and are ambushed by Black Sun agents, helped by Anja Gallandro, a lightsaber-wielding non-Jedi who blames Han for her father's death, though Solo reveals her father died in a trap. In Trouble on Cloud City, Czethros is revealed as a minor Black Sun leader trying to gain power, and Jacen, Tenel Ka, and Lowbacca are ambushed, with Jacen nearly killed. In Crisis at Crystal Reef, Jaina attempts to capture Czethros while Jacen helps Anja overcome her spice addiction and fight Black Sun; Anja recovers and accepts her father's death, and Jacen realizes she lacks Jedi potential, ending his infatuation when she joins Lando. In the New Jedi Order series, Luke takes Jacen as his apprentice, though they disagree on philosophical issues; Jacen believes the Force is a guide to destiny and tells Anakin that the Force is part of something greater. During the Yuuzhan Vong attack in Dark Tide: Onslaught, Jacen believes many Jedi are too aggressive and temporarily abandons his powers, but returns to battle due to his love for his mother, eventually making peace with his father. In Star by Star, Jacen joins a mission to Myrkr to infiltrate a Yuuzhan Vong cloning facility where the invaders create Voxyn; the mission fails with Anakin's death, and Jacen, forced into leadership, uses the Force Meld to unite the team. After destroying the voxyn queen, Jacen is captured by the Yuuzhan Vong under Vergere and Nom Anor, disappearing from the Force. In Traitor, he awakens in the Embrace of Pain, where he learns to use pain to sustain himself under Vergere's tutelage, who was once a Jedi of the Old Republic and met his grandfather, Anakin Skywalker. He works on Yuuzhan Vong ships, heals slaves, and uses a slave seed beneath his flesh to communicate with their technology, escaping by commanding amphistaffs to surround him. Jacen and Vergere flee to Coruscant, where the planet is transformed into a Yuuzhan Vong paradise. Vergere removes the slave seed, but Jacen still senses the Yuuzhan Vong; he is surrounded by warriors, channels Force lightning, runs away, and is later given full Force use by Vergere. He surrenders and becomes the "khattazz al'Yun," or Avatar of God, with Nom Anor intending to use him to sacrifice Jaina, fulfilling a prophecy. Jacen's true allegiance remains his own; when ordered to sacrifice Jedi Ganner Rhysode, he refuses and instead helps Ganner hold off the Yuuzhan Vong, confronting the World Brain and suggesting it work against the invaders. Ganner dies, but Jacen escapes with Vergere. He returns to the New Republic as a hardened man, joins Admiral Kre'fey's fleet, and participates in a successful deception at Ebaq 9, where Vergere dies. Her spectral form appears to him afterward. As the Galactic Alliance forms, Jacen accompanies Luke into the Unknown Regions to seek a solution to the Yuuzhan Vong threat, playing a key role in finding Zonama Sekot and convincing the planet to join the fight. He kills Supreme Overlord Onimi, using the Force as a conduit, after nearly being killed by Shimrra, and begins to believe he is beyond good and evil, marking the start of his fall. After the war ends, Jacen tells Luke he plans to travel the galaxy to learn more about the Force. On a five-year journey, he enters a realm of the Force known as beyond shadows, trained by a sect called the Mind Walkers, and gazes into the Pool of Knowledge, which holds the Throne of Balance, where all future events are shown. He sees a dark man ruling the galaxy and becomes determined to prevent this future. Following this, Jacen begins his descent into the dark side. In Dark Nest, he feels a Force urge, follows his sister to the Unknown Regions to help the Killik against a Chiss invasion, returns to Galactic Alliance space, and travels to the Hapes Cluster to ask Tenel Ka to assist with the conflict, sending a fleet of Hapan Battle Dragons to protect the Killiks. In The Unseen Queen, Tenel Ka gives birth to his daughter, Allana, who is attacked by the Gorog; Jacen repels the attack, uses the Force to send Tenel Ka's grandmother into a coma, and sees a vision of a never-ending war with the Killiks at its center. Determined to prevent it, he provokes the Chiss into destroying the Killiks, though he later reveals he does not know who started the war in the vision. In The Swarm War, Luke follows Jacen's advice, including when Jacen tells him he is not ready to face Lomi Plo, the Dark Queen of the Gorog. Jacen, with R2-D2, helps Luke confront his fears about Mara's involvement in his mother's death and accompanies him to face Plo. During the fight, Luke falters when Mara is injured, Plo holds him, and Jacen is critically wounded while saving Mara's life; Mara injures Plo and tends to Jacen's wounds. While recovering, Jacen urges Luke to embrace his darker emotions, but Luke refuses and defeats Plo and Raynar Thul without using the dark side. In the novel, Jacen watches holovideos of his grandparents, Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala, seeing Anakin fall to the dark side and Padmé die in childbirth due to Anakin's actions; Jacen sympathizes with Anakin's desire to protect his wife and reminds Luke that Anakin was a fallible human. In Betrayal, Jacen begins training his cousin Ben in the Force. After a mission to Adumar ends in a life-threatening attack, they return to a dinner party at their parents' home, where Han expresses concern over Corellia's independence. Luke orders Jacen and Ben to disable the Centerpoint Station, which Thrackan Sal-Solo, Han's cousin, is using; Ben disables it while Jacen distracts Thrackan, ensuring a partial victory. While traveling to a subterranean base, Ben and Nelani are forced out of a mining car; their guide, Brisha Syo, creates a dark side phantom of Luke that nearly kills Jacen. Brisha stops the projections and takes Jacen to an office where Darth Vectivus, the supposed Sith Lord, lives. After fighting Force projections with Ben, Nelani catches up with them. Brisha is revealed to be Lumiya, the Dark Lady of the Sith, who reveals that Vergere is a Sith apprentice and that Jacen has already received Sith training. Lumiya claims Jacen will become the next Sith Lord. Unsure of his next move, Jacen creates visions of the future; in each vision where Lumiya is arrested, the galaxy falls into endless war and Jacen ends up fighting Luke. Horrified, Jacen spares Lumiya. Nelani attempts to arrest her, but Jacen intervenes, realizing she might fulfill the dark vision, and fights and kills her, asking for forgiveness before striking her down. He agrees to consider Lumiya's claims and leaves the asteroid with an unconscious Ben, erasing Ben's memories of Lumiya and Nelani, telling him both were killed by dark side phantoms. They return to Coruscant, but after Jacen departs, Lumiya says she has won. In Bloodlines, fully pledged to Lumiya, Jacen becomes head of the Galactic Alliance Guard, begins rounding up Corellians for internment, and during an interrogation of a suspected assassin (Ailyn Vel, Boba Fett's daughter), accidentally kills her using the Force. In Tempest, Jacen takes command of Rogue Squadron during the blockade of Corellia, shoots down a civilian freighter that had fired on him, relieves his sister from duty for refusing to participate, and uses the Anakin Solo to fire upon the Millennium Falcon, while both his sister and he are involved.

Jacen Solo, after agreeing to consider Lumiya's words and leaving the asteroid with an unconscious Ben, erases Ben's memories of Lumiya and tells him both she and Nelani were killed by dark side phantoms. They return to Coruscant, where after Jacen departs, Lumiya claims she has won. In Bloodlines, fully pledged to Lumiya, Jacen becomes head of the GFFA's secret police, the Galactic Alliance Guard, and, with Ben at his side, begins rounding up Corellians for internment and deportation. During an interrogation of a suspected assassin—Ailyn Vel, Boba Fett's daughter—Jacen attempts to use the Force to extract information and accidentally kills her. In Tempest, Jacen takes command of Rogue Squadron during the blockade of Corellia, shoots down a civilian freighter that had fired on him, relieves his sister from duty for refusing to participate, and uses the Anakin Solo to fire upon the Millennium Falcon while both his sister and parents are on board. He believes his parents were involved in a failed assassination of Tenel Ka, when in fact they were set up by Dur Gejjen, Prime Minister of Corellia. In Sacrifice, Lumiya says she is pleased with his progress and instructs him to undergo the Trial of Sacrifice—to kill what he loves most—believing this would allow him to use Sith powers without becoming evil and "immortalize his love" through sacrifice. Jacen decides the only way is to kill Tenel Ka and their daughter Allana. After Ben overhears Jacen communicating with Lumiya, Mara Jade tracks him down in the Hapes Consortium, where they fight in a long and heated battle, and Jacen kills Mara. The sacrifice required to become a Sith Lord is not Jacen's love, but Ben's. Ben suspects Jacen immediately upon meeting him at his mother's body. Eventually, Jacen chooses the Sith name Darth Caedus. By Fury, Darth Caedus becomes the principal antagonist, declared enemy of nearly every major character, including his parents, sister, Luke, and Ben. He kidnaps Allana to prevent Tenel Ka and the Hapans from leaving government, but Han, Leia, Luke, Jaina, Ben, and allies save her. After saving Allana, Leia tells Caedus to become a Jedi again, but he refuses. Han and Leia later discover Allana is Caedus and Tenel Ka's child. In Revelation, Caedus takes Tahiri Veila as his new apprentice to replace Ben and turns to ending the war, enticing the Imperial Remnant to attack Fondor. Though Admiral Niathal offers Fondor a chance to surrender, Caedus insists on making an example of it by crippling its shipyards and government. After sharing military secrets that cause hundreds of deaths and compromise the battle plan, Niathal arranges a cease-fire without consulting Caedus. Enraged by the treason, Caedus orders the fleet to ignore Niathal's orders and bombard major cities. Niathal orders ships loyal to her to attack the Anakin Solo. Two-thirds of the fleet sides with Caedus, while the rest ally with Niathal. When the Imperial Remnant refuses to assist Caedus, his apprentice assassinates Imperial Head of State Gilad Pellaeon and transfers control to the Moffs, who then support Jacen. A mysterious fleet led by Admiral Daala, loyal to Pellaeon, appears with one hundred Mandalorian mercenaries and, due to Daala's experimental weapons, forces the Galactic Alliance Fleet into retreat. Caedus then takes control of Coruscant and claims sole control of the Galactic Alliance. In Invincible, Jaina takes it upon herself to defeat her brother. Caedus's meditations are disrupted by Luke Skywalker, who attempts to hide Jaina's attack. Jaina, with several Mandalorian commandos, confronts Caedus, who quickly dispatches the Mandalorians while Jaina acts as a sniper. When she runs out of ammunition, she seizes a Mandalorian saber and severs Caedus's arm. Jaina withdraws due to her own injuries. After escaping an attack by Luke on the Anakin Solo's bridge, Caedus sees a vision of his daughter Allana on a white throne in a time of peace, which convinces him he has won—bringing peace to the galaxy and preventing future war and suffering. At the climax, Caedus and Jaina face off in a final lightsaber duel aboard the Anakin Solo. During the duel, Caedus returns to the light and tries to persuade Jaina of his intentions to protect Tenel Ka and Allana, but she refuses to listen and attacks after he deactivates and holsters his lightsaber. She later slams the door shut when he tries to leave. After a grueling battle in which both are seriously injured, Jacen is defeated when Jaina severs his Achilles tendon and stabs him in the heart. As he dies, Jacen reaches out to both his former lover and his child through the Force, warning them to flee from a bio-warfare attack designed by the Imperial Remnant. In this act of selflessness, Jaina sees the remnants of the good man her brother had once been. Following Caedus's death and the war's end, the Galactic Alliance defeats the Confederation and peace is restored to the galaxy, as Jacen had foreseen in a Force vision. Though Jacen makes few true appearances in Fate of the Jedi, which follows the Legacy of the Force series, his legacy is felt throughout, as Luke Skywalker is arrested for negligence of duty and sentenced to a ten-year exile, during which he and Ben investigate how and why Jacen turned to the dark side. Jacen's spirit makes its first appearance in Abyss, where it warns Luke and Ben about Abeloth, the main antagonist. In the final novel, Apocalypse, Jacen's spirit (along with Mara's) aids Luke as he partners with Darth Krayt in the final battle against Abeloth. After Abeloth is destroyed, Jacen reveals that Krayt was the dark figure he saw in his vision of the future and the source of his downfall; he saw Allana standing next to Krayt. In response, Krayt insists that Caedus's actions merely delayed the Sith, who will eventually succeed in their planned takeover of the galaxy. In aiding the Jedi against Abeloth, Jacen posthumously redeems himself, though he still refers to his fate as damnation. While Luke does not forgive his nephew for his role in Mara's death, he gains understanding of what led Jacen to that point. The second volume of the Legacy comic series, set about 140 years after Return of the Jedi, features Jacen's descendant Ania Solo as the protagonist. In this era, the descendants of Jacen, Jaina, and Ben are main characters, set during and after Darth Krayt takes over the galaxy. Though they do not appear as spirits, older characters like Luke and Mara do. IGN listed Jacen as #17 on their list of the top 100 Star Wars heroes, noting he had a more "profound effect" than any other Solo child on the Star Wars setting. Jesse Schedeen, writing for IGN, also listed Darth Caedus as #5 in a reader-inspired list of top Star Wars villains, calling his "defining moment of villainy" his murder of Mara Jade. UGO.com listed Jacen as their top Star Wars expanded universe character, calling him "one of the most fearsome - and most tragic - villains in the Star Wars universe." With the release of Star Wars: The Force Awakens in production in April 2014, most licensed Star Wars novels and comics produced since 1977 were declared non-canon. The epilogue of "Family Reunion – and Farewell," the series finale of Star Wars Rebels, introduces a character named Jacen Syndulla by series creator Dave Filoni in honor of Jacen Solo.
